target.title: improve(imessage): manage imsg setup and plugin skill ownership
target.body:
Related: openclaw/imsg#157

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where OpenClaw's bundled iMessage guidance and setup flow lagged the current `imsg` CLI: the OpenClaw copy of the `imsg` skill still lived outside the iMessage plugin, did not document the landed poll behavior, and setup only reported that `imsg` was missing without offering the Homebrew install/update path most local Mac users need.

This is AI-assisted work.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `imsg` skill now lives with the bundled iMessage plugin, matching the existing Discord, Slack, WhatsApp, and QQBot channel-plugin pattern. The old top-level `skills/imsg` copy was removed.

The iMessage setup flow borrows the Signal-style prepare hook to offer macOS Homebrew install/update for the default local `imsg` path, while preserving explicit custom `cliPath` values, including SSH/PATH wrappers. Probe and setup status messages now distinguish default/Homebrew-managed `imsg` from operator-owned wrappers, and doctor can repair stale session snapshot paths to the generated plugin-skill path when that path has been published.

Clanker checked the prior Vincent/Jason history: Vincent previously moved bundled skills into plugin directories with manifest `skills` entries and did not add extra doctor migration. This PR keeps that ownership move, with a conservative doctor repair only for stale session metadata when the generated plugin-skill target exists.

Codex review note: local Codex review repeatedly flagged that moving `imsg` into plugin skills means the skill is only published when the iMessage plugin is activated. I am keeping that behavior because Omar explicitly asked to remove the old skill and align with other channel plugins; the PR body calls out the tradeoff for maintainer review.

## User Impact

Users configuring iMessage on the signed-in Messages Mac can install or update `imsg` from setup instead of manually discovering the command. Existing custom wrapper/SSH setups are left untouched, and setup/probe errors point operators at the configured wrapper when that is what is missing.

Agents using the iMessage skill get updated poll guidance, including the landed `imsg poll send` caption behavior and poll history/watch backfill notes.

target.title: [codex] Keep ambiguous delivery attempts recoverable
target.body:
## Summary

- Keeps outbound delivery entries in ambiguous post-send states pending when adapter reconciliation is unavailable.
- Preserves the existing no-blind-replay behavior while leaving the entry retryable for later reconciliation/backoff.
- Avoids consuming retry budget when no reconciliation-capable adapter ran, so ambiguous entries do not age into terminal failure before a later adapter can reconcile them.
- Treats a reconciliation-capable adapter returning `null` as a completed unresolved reconciliation attempt, so that path still consumes retry budget and respects the max-retry cap.
- Updates startup recovery, reconnect-drain, and outbound queue integration coverage plus Discord troubleshooting guidance for #87544.

## Scope

This is a narrow mitigation for #87544 and intentionally does not close the full issue. The broader transcript-to-provider delivery ledger, Discord reconciliation semantics, and UI/API surfacing still need maintainer design.

## Validation

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

target.title: feat(memory): carry source actor context into recall
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Memory recall can currently receive the conversation/session context without a stable indication of which group participant authored the triggering message. In multi-person channels, that can make retrieved or promoted memory read as if another participant's facts belong to the operator. This PR carries the generic source actor context into memory recall and prompt supplements so memory backends can preserve participant attribution without adding backend-specific logic.

## Summary

- Carries `SourceActor` from inbound context through embedded runs and plugin tool context.
- Exposes the same source actor context to memory corpus supplements for `memory_search` and `memory_get`.
- Reuses the typed `SourceActorRole` contract across reply runtime, plugin tool context, and memory context.
- Adds memory prompt/flush guidance to preserve participant attribution instead of merging another participant's facts into the operator/user profile.

## Scope and honesty

This PR carries `SourceActor` context into memory recall and adds prompt/flush guidance to preserve participant attribution. It is the plumbing + guidance layer: it makes attribution available and instructs the model to keep it. It does NOT yet structurally enforce attribution on stored memories (e.g., tagging persisted entries with the source actor) -- that is a follow-up. Best-effort: recall tracking never blocks recall.

## Stack

This is stacked after #96738, `codex/signal-mention-facts-context`, and `codex/source-actor-context-contract`. Until those land, this PR's diff will include its dependencies. Merge order should stay #96738 -> #96862 -> #96863 -> #96864, with later PRs rebased after earlier ones land.

## Diff shape

- Contract: source actor context and typed role reuse across reply/plugin/memory SDK types.
- Agent plumbing: inbound `SourceActor` is carried into embedded runs and plugin tool context.
- Memory core: `memory_search`/`memory_get` receive `sourceActor`; prompt/flush guidance mentions participant attribution.
- Signal prerequisite: mention context exposes delivered-turn mention facts only; skipped Signal turns do not create public prompt/tool context.
- Tests: channel/source actor parity, agent plugin context, auto-reply runner utils, memory-core source actor paths.
- Docs/API: channel plugin docs plus plugin SDK API baseline hash update.

## Production impact

No storage migration and no backend-specific behavior. This is not Honcho-specific: it adds a generic runtime/tool/memory contract that memory backends and supplements can consume. Core memory search still filters by existing session/source visibility; this PR does not claim a new per-person storage partition.

target.title: fix(signal): detect native bot mentions in group gating
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Signal groups can be configured with `requireMention=true` so side chatter stays quiet until the bot is explicitly mentioned. Signal native mentions arrive as structured `dataMessage.mentions[]` metadata plus object-replacement characters in the message text. The current Signal handler renders those placeholders as `@<uuid>` or `@<phone>`, then relies on text mention regexes. Selecting the bot from Signal's native mention UI can therefore fail to wake the bot unless a matching text fallback happens to be configured.

This also leaves `canDetectMention` tied only to configured text regexes and passes `hasAnyMention=false` even when Signal supplied structured mention metadata.

## Why This Change Was Made

This patch keeps the fix inside the Signal plugin and adds a small native mention fact resolver. It compares structured Signal mention metadata against the current bot account identity:

- UUID via `channels.signal.accountUuid`
- phone number via the existing E.164 normalizer and `channels.signal.account`

The event handler now combines text fallback and native metadata:

- `wasMentioned` is true for text fallback or a native mention that targets the current bot account.
- `canDetectMention` reflects text regexes or available bot account identity.
- `hasAnyMention` reflects valid structured Signal mention metadata so the shared mention-decision contract can distinguish command bypass from messages mentioning someone else.

Mentions of other participants do not trigger the bot. Missing bot identity does not become a false mention. Existing text fallback, group access checks, pending history, attachment restraint, control-command handling, direct messages, and `requireMention=false` behavior stay unchanged.

This supersedes #69413, which was closed without merge, by adding the missing capability facts, event-handler coverage, and docs.

## User Impact

Before:

> A user could select the bot from Signal's native mention UI in a `requireMention` group and get no response because the rendered `@uuid`/`@phone` text did not match the configured agent-name regex.

After:

> Native Signal mentions targeting the current bot account pass mention gating. Mentions of other participants remain silent and are kept only as bounded pending context. A later bot mention can include recent skipped group context and reply in the same group.

Docs now describe Signal native mention behavior, `accountUuid`, text mention fallback, and a mention-gated group configuration with bounded history.

### Behavior Change

Signal groups with `requireMention=true` that have a configured bot identity (`accountUuid`/`account`) but no text mention regexes previously fell through to pass-through handling. After this change they enforce mention gating via native Signal mention metadata. Group chatter that did not mention the bot but previously reached it may now be gated. This is intended and makes native-only `requireMention` groups behave as documented. Maintainers with such groups should expect stricter, correct gating after upgrade.

### Trust Model

`dataMessage.mentions[]` is sender-supplied. A group member could craft metadata naming the bot; the only effect is waking the bot, which any member can already do via a normal Signal mention. Native facts are still validated against a real object-replacement placeholder span, so malformed metadata does not become a bot mention.

### Native Identity Note

For full native mention coverage, configure `channels.signal.accountUuid` alongside `channels.signal.account`. Phone-only identity can still match phone-backed mention metadata, but UUID-only Signal mention metadata requires `accountUuid`.

## Evidence

- Base: `4ecb45b chore: update default check gate expectations`
- Head: `83ac15c979a4`
- Static whitespace check: `git diff --check HEAD~1..HEAD`
- Focused Signal mention-gating tests passed on this branch:
  `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.mention-gating.test.ts`
- Production TypeScript check passed:
  `pnpm tsgo:prod`

The focused Signal suite covers:

- native bot UUID mention without text mention patterns;
- native bot phone mention with E.164 normalization;
- native mention of another participant stays silent and records pending context;
- malformed matching metadata does not become a bot mention;
- no-detector behavior remains explicit;
- helper facts for bot mention, unrelated mention, malformed span, and missing bot identity.

### Redacted Live Signal Proof

This is the sanitized inspectable artifact from a live 3-person private Signal smoke. IDs, UUIDs, phone numbers, group IDs, raw message bodies, and private participant context are intentionally omitted.

observed: no bot reply was produced after the quiet window

## What Problem This Solves

Signal group mention gating now has native mention metadata available, but the delivered-turn decision facts are only visible inside the Signal monitor. Downstream prompt/tool context cannot inspect whether the inbound group message had native mention metadata, whether `requireMention` was enforced for that delivered turn, or which mention path matched the bot. ## Stack

This is stacked after #96738 (`fix(signal): detect native bot mentions in group gating`). Until #96738 lands, this PR's diff will include that dependency.

## Production impact

No new outbound behavior. This only makes already-computed delivered-turn mention gating facts inspectable by prompts, tests, and plugin/channel contracts. target.title: fix(acpx): handle target stdout stream errors
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where ACPX-backed MCP proxy sessions could crash with an unhandled stream error when the proxied target stdout stream emits an error.

## Why This Change Was Made

The proxy already routes target stdin, proxy stdout, and child process errors through one controlled failure path. This change applies the same local boundary handling to the target stdout stream before piping it to the proxy stdout, without changing ACPX command rewriting or MCP payload behavior.

## User Impact

ACPX MCP proxy failures from target stdout streams now exit cleanly with the underlying error instead of surfacing as an unhandled Node stream error.

## Evidence

- Maintainer follow-up proof (2026-07-08): removed the leading UTF-8 BOM from this PR body so `scripts/github/real-behavior-proof-check.mjs` can recognize the existing `## What Problem This Solves` heading. target.title: fix(web): avoid exact-limit fetch truncation warnings
target.body:
﻿Closes #101837

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running `web_fetch` could see a response reported as truncated when the streamed response body was exactly `maxResponseBytes` bytes, even though no bytes were omitted.

## Why This Change Was Made

`readResponseText` now treats truncation as proven only when a chunk exceeds the remaining byte budget. Reaching the byte budget exactly no longer flips the truncation flag by itself, so exact-limit responses can complete normally while true overflow still cancels the reader.

## User Impact

Users no longer get misleading `Response body truncated after ... bytes.` warnings for complete responses that happen to land exactly on the byte cap. Oversized responses are still bounded and marked truncated.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: Current head `18b610b93e7e0a96de0eb891de3bab0e43f2c74b` lets an exact-limit `readResponseText` helper run complete without setting `truncated`, while still reporting the exact byte count.
- Real helper proof for the requested boundary, constructing a real `Response` from streamed chunks `"hello"` + `" world"` and reading it with `maxBytes: 11`:
  ```text
  node --import ../openclaw/node_modules/tsx/dist/esm/index.mjs --input-type=module -e "import { readResponseText } from './src/agents/tools/web-shared.ts'; const encoder = new TextEncoder(); let cancelCount = 0; const response = new Response(new ReadableStream({ start(controller) { controller.enqueue(encoder.encode('hello')); controller.enqueue(encoder.encode(' world')); controller.close(); }, cancel() { cancelCount += 1; } })); const result = await readResponseText(response, { maxBytes: 11 }); console.log(JSON.stringify({ text: result.text, truncated: result.truncated, bytesRead: result.bytesRead, cancelCount }));"
  {"text":"hello world","truncated":false,"bytesRead":11,"cancelCount":0}
  ```
- Focused regression: `PNPM_CONFIG_MODULES_DIR='../openclaw/node_modules' node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/web-shared.test.ts` passed (`1` file, `12` tests).
- Whitespace check: `git diff --check` passed.
- GitHub current-head checks: `gh pr checks 101845 --repo openclaw/openclaw --json name,bucket,state,completedAt,link` showed no failed buckets; current checks are pass/skip/neutral.
- Duplicate search before issue creation: no open issue or PR found for `web_fetch truncated maxBytes exact limit` or `readResponseText truncated maxBytes`.

Observed result: exact-limit helper output is `truncated:false`, `bytesRead:11`, and `cancelCount:0`, so the shared helper no longer feeds a false truncation warning to `web_fetch` for complete exact-cap responses.

target.title: fix: guard generated video downloads [AI]
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users generating videos from providers that return URL-only assets could have the CLI download provider-supplied URLs without applying the configured provider request network policy.

## Why This Change Was Made

The CLI now resolves the selected provider's request policy for URL-only generated video assets and downloads them through the guarded provider HTTP path. This preserves streaming output and in-memory size caps while keeping provider request config as the opt-in path for private-network downloads.

## User Impact

CLI video generation keeps working for normal provider-hosted media, blocks private/internal download targets by default, and still permits configured private-network providers when operators opt into that request policy.

Release-note-style behavior note: URL-only generated video downloads that resolve to private/internal networks now fail closed unless the selected provider already has `models.providers.<provider>.request.allowPrivateNetwork` enabled.

## Evidence

- AI-assisted.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/capability-cli.test.ts` passed: 108 tests.

target.title: fix: reject zero cron failure alert cooldowns
target.body:
Closes #101770

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `openclaw cron edit --failure-alert-cooldown 0.1ms` could save a `0ms` failure-alert cooldown even though the user entered a positive-looking duration.

## Why This Change Was Made

The cron edit path now rejects parsed cooldown values that are falsy, matching the duration parser's invalid result for tiny durations that floor to `0ms`.

## User Impact

Users configuring cron failure alerts get a clear validation error instead of accidentally disabling cooldown throttling.

## Evidence

Head SHA: `ebf57fadad370ad297867443a5d6dd425218c026`

Changed files:
- `src/cli/cron-cli/register.cron-edit.ts`
- `src/cli/cron-cli.test.ts`

Claim proved:
- `cron edit --failure-alert-cooldown 0.1ms` is rejected before `cron.update`, so tiny positive durations that floor to `0ms` are not saved.

Commands / observed results:
- `PNPM_CONFIG_MODULES_DIR=E:\code\openclaw\node_modules node scripts/run-node.mjs cron edit job-1 --failure-alert-cooldown 0.1ms; Write-Host "EXIT_CODE=$LASTEXITCODE"`
  - Output included `Error: Invalid --failure-alert-cooldown.` and `EXIT_CODE=1` on head `ebf57fadad370ad297867443a5d6dd425218c026`.
- `PNPM_CONFIG_MODULES_DIR=E:\code\openclaw\node_modules CI=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/cron-cli.test.ts`
  - Passed: 1 file / 104 tests.
- Focused CLI-shard proof also passed for `rejects failure alert cooldowns that floor to zero on cron edit`; that regression runs `cron edit job-1 --failure-alert-cooldown 0.1ms`, asserts `Invalid --failure-alert-cooldown`, and asserts `cron.update` is not called.
- `git diff --check`
  - Passed with no output.

Autoreview:
- Current follow-up run used the configured `pixel_api` relay and returned `no local changes to review`; no new diff was added in this proof refresh.

Closes #101770

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `openclaw cron edit --failure-alert-cooldown 0.1ms` could save a `0ms` failure-alert cooldown even though the user entered a positive-looking duration.

## Why This Change Was Made

The cron edit path now rejects parsed cooldown values that are falsy, matching the duration parser's invalid result for tiny durations that floor to `0ms`.

## User Impact

Users configuring cron failure alerts get a clear validation error instead of accidentally disabling cooldown throttling.

target.title: fix: require exact markdown frontmatter fences

Closes #101769

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Markdown that starts with dash-prefixed text such as `---not` or `----` could be treated as a frontmatter block.

## Why This Change Was Made

Frontmatter parsing, bundled command body stripping, and skill workshop proposal stripping now require opening and closing fences to be whole `---` lines. This keeps ordinary dash-prefixed Markdown content from being parsed or stripped as metadata.

target.title: fix(auth): prioritize explicit models.json apiKey over store profiles
target.body:
> [!NOTE]
> **AI-Assisted Contribution:** This PR was prepared and validated with the assistance of an AI coding assistant (Antigravity/Gemini).

## What Problem This Solves
Resolves a problem where the model auth subsystem ignores explicit `apiKey` (literal or SecretRef) overrides in `models.json` if store profiles exist (pr #100839).

**Symptom/Behavior:**
1. Unless `auth: "api-key"` is explicitly set (making `shouldPreferExplicitConfigApiKeyAuth` true), the literal key or SecretRef configured in `models.json` is ignored during the binding phase (falling through `providerEntryBinding` checks). The function then scans the profile store; if any profile is found for the provider, it overrides the user's explicit `apiKey` configuration.
2. Additionally, when a specific profile was requested (e.g. during failover rotation or pinned session), the early check for explicit models.json `apiKey` would bypass profile resolution entirely and return the models.json `apiKey` instead of the rotated profile, causing E2E failover tests (`rotates for overloaded assistant failures across auto-pinned profiles`) to fail.
3. In `models status` and `models auth list` commands, placeholder/marker values in the environment (e.g. `GOOGLE_API_KEY`) were treated as literal keys, causing incorrect `effective=models.json` formatting instead of falling back to store profiles.

Affected locations:
- [resolveApiKeyForProvider](file:///home/dietpi/Developer/openclaw/src/agents/model-auth.ts#L1071-L1084)
- [resolveProviderAuthOverview](file:///home/dietpi/Developer/openclaw/src/commands/models/list.auth-overview.ts#L152-L163)

## Why This Change Was Made
Implemented a surgical fix to resolve the logic discrepancy and test failures:
1. Updated `resolveApiKeyForProvider` to only check and return the configured `apiKey` (either a literal key or a resolved SecretRef) if `profileId` is NOT explicitly requested (`if (!params.profileId && !params.lockedProfile)`).
2. Refactored `isLiteral` in `src/commands/models/list.auth-overview.ts` to exclude non-secret placeholder/marker values using `!isNonSecretApiKeyMarker(...)`, and adjusted the precedence logic so that env-var markers do not override the effective auth early, allowing correct fallback to profiles/env.
3. Updated `resolveUsableCustomProviderApiKey` in `src/agents/model-auth.ts` to correctly filter out environment-resolved placeholder markers.

---

## User Impact
Corrects behavior to ensure that:
1. If a user configures `apiKey` in `models.json` under `models.providers.[provider].apiKey` as a literal API key string or a SecretRef, this configured credential takes precedence over any general auth profiles in the store, unless a specific profile is requested/rotated.
2. In user-facing CLI commands (`models status`), actual placeholder markers correctly fall back to database profiles in format outputs.

---

## Evidence

### Unit Tests / Verification Suite

target.title: add per-conversation whatsapp debounce config
target.body:
## Summary

Adds per-conversation inbound debounce configuration for WhatsApp direct chats and groups.

Practically, this controls how long OpenClaw waits before starting an agent turn after receiving a WhatsApp message from a specific conversation. This is useful when a contact sends multiple messages in a row: OpenClaw can wait a few seconds or minutes, collect the full burst, and then let the agent process the conversation with better context.

## What Problem This Solves

The existing WhatsApp debounce setting is too broad for mixed usage.

Some conversations should be processed immediately, while others should wait briefly:

- owner/admin chats often need immediate processing, so they can use `debounceMs: 0`
- external contacts often send multiple short messages in a row, so they can use a longer debounce, such as `180000`, to wait 3 minutes
- noisy groups can have their own debounce window
- wildcard entries can define defaults for all direct chats or all groups

This lets operators tune batching by conversation without changing the global WhatsApp debounce for every chat.

## Behavior

- supports `debounceMs` in `channels.whatsapp.direct`
- supports `debounceMs` in `channels.whatsapp.groups`
- supports wildcard entries like `direct["*"]` and `groups["*"]`
- specific conversation config wins over wildcard config
- falls back to the existing global WhatsApp debounce when no conversation override exists
- `debounceMs: 0` disables debounce for that conversation only

## Evidence

Redacted real WhatsApp setup proof from a local OpenClaw home:

The run used the PR branch plus real WhatsApp session keys from the local OpenClaw session index. The proof output prints only counts and redacted aliases; it does not include phone numbers, group JIDs, contact names, credentials, or message bodies. It feeds those real direct/group session keys through the same keyed inbound debouncer that the WhatsApp listener calls through `resolveDebounceMs`.

```text
$ node --import tsx <redacted local proof script>
   0ms real-session-inventory direct=200 group=3
   0ms config <redacted-direct-1> debounceMs=0
   0ms config <redacted-direct-2> debounceMs=120
   0ms config <redacted-group-1> debounceMs=180
   0ms flush <redacted-direct-1> items=1 debounceMs=0
   0ms flush <redacted-direct-1> items=1 debounceMs=0
 151ms flush <redacted-direct-2> items=2 debounceMs=120
 220ms flush <redacted-group-1> items=2 debounceMs=180
# exit code 0
```

This shows the changed batching behavior with real WhatsApp conversation identifiers redacted: the `debounceMs: 0` direct override flushes two messages immediately as separate items, while the other direct conversation and the group conversation batch two quick messages into one flush using their own per-conversation windows.

target.title: fix(agents): avoid false unscheduled note after shell cron add
target.body:
Closes #52972

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users who schedule reminders through a shell-driven `openclaw cron add ...` command could still receive the false note saying no reminder was scheduled in the turn.

## Why This Change Was Made

The reminder guard already trusts successful structured `cron` tool adds. This extends the same producer-side counter to successful `exec` and `bash` commands that run `openclaw cron add` and return a cron add response shaped like the CLI output.

The repair also handles the CLI warning path where `openclaw cron add --message ...` emits the missing-agent warning on stderr while still printing the successful JSON receipt on stdout. Exec aggregates stdout and stderr, so the parser now scans the aggregate for a valid cron-add JSON receipt instead of requiring the whole aggregate to be pure JSON. Failed commands and unrelated cron commands are ignored.

## User Impact

Users no longer get a contradictory unscheduled-reminder note after a shell cron add succeeds, including the default-agent warning case. Failed or unrelated shell commands still leave the guard active.

## Evidence

Redacted behavior proof, run from the PR checkout after rebasing on current `main`:

```text
command=openclaw cron add --at +1h --message <redacted> --name reminder
aggregateContainsWarning=true
aggregateContainsJsonReceipt=true
successfulCronAdds=1
hasReminderCommitment=true
falseNotePresent=false
deliveredReply=I'll remind you in an hour.
```

The proof used the production tool lifecycle handlers with a mixed warning-plus-JSON exec aggregate, then applied the production reminder-guard decision to the delivered reply payload.

target.title: fix(gateway): bound BOOT.md file read size
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`loadBootFile` in `src/gateway/boot.ts` read the workspace `BOOT.md` with an unbounded `fs.readFile`, allowing an arbitrarily large file to be loaded into memory during gateway boot.

## Why This Change Was Made

Switch to `readRegularFile` from `../infra/regular-file.js` with a 16 MiB cap, matching the pattern used for other bounded file reads. The helper also rejects symlinks and non-file targets. An oversized `BOOT.md` is treated as empty/missing so the boot step is skipped safely instead of failing or allocating excessive memory.

## User Impact

No behavioral change for normal `BOOT.md` files. Pathologically large `BOOT.md` files are now handled safely and consistently: the boot check is skipped rather than attempting an unbounded read.

## Evidence

- Added regression test in `src/gateway/boot.test.ts` that creates a `16 MiB + 1` byte `BOOT.md` and asserts `runBootOnce` returns `{ status: "skipped", reason: "empty" }`.
- Local focused run: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/boot.test.ts --run` passes (68/68 tests across gateway configs).
- `oxlint` clean on changed files.

## Real behavior proof

target.body:
## Summary

Stacked after #101328. This adds the first read-only Claw feed layer so OpenClaw can discover a Claw from a feed entry and build the same lifecycle plan introduced in PR2.

Design reference: RFC PR https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/27

- adds `openclaw.clawFeed.v1` types, strict parsing, and local feed file reading
- resolves feed entries to local Claw manifest sources with source-locality checks
- adds owner/trust metadata on feed entries and warnings for missing owner evidence
- adds `openclaw claws feed inspect <feed>` and `openclaw claws feed plan <feed> <claw>`
- keeps PR3 read-only: remote feed fetch, install, mutation, and ClawHub publish/search stay deferred

## Safety / ownership behavior

- relative feed sources must stay under the feed file directory
- absolute local paths are rejected
- remote `http`/`https` sources are rejected in this PR
- `file:` URLs are accepted only if they resolve under the feed directory
- feed entry id must match the resolved manifest id
- feed entry version mismatch is diagnostic-only warning so feeds can surface drift without mutating anything

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/claws/schema.test.ts src/claws/feed.test.ts src/cli/claws-cli.test.ts src/cli/program/command-registry.test.ts src/cli/program/root-command-descriptions.test.ts`

This PR adds read-only local Claw feed inspection and feed-to-Claw planning so OpenClaw can parse an `openclaw.clawFeed.v1` file, resolve a local Claw manifest entry under the feed directory, and emit the same read-only Claw plan shape from PR2 without installing or mutating state.

target.title: fix(discord): split encoded video URLs from captions
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a Discord outbound send edge case where a caption + video URL can miss the existing caption-first/media-second split when the URL encodes the extension dot, such as `render%2Emp4`.

The split decision depends on Discord's local video URL classification. `new URL(...).pathname` preserves `%2E`, so a path like `/attachments/1/render%2Emp4` did not match the existing `.mp4` / `.webm` / `.mov` suffix check and was treated as non-video.

## Why This Change Was Made

The production change is intentionally small and stays inside Discord's local media detector:

```diff
 const parsed = new URL(trimmed);
-return normalizeLowercaseStringOrEmpty(parsed.pathname);
+try {
+  return normalizeLowercaseStringOrEmpty(decodeURIComponent(parsed.pathname));
+} catch {
+  return normalizeLowercaseStringOrEmpty(parsed.pathname);
+}
```

This decodes URL pathnames before video-extension matching, while preserving the previous fallback for malformed percent encoding. Local non-URL paths still use the existing query/hash stripping path, and the original `mediaUrl` is still passed through to the Discord send call.

## User Impact

Discord outbound sends with a caption and an encoded video extension now follow the same behavior covered by the existing video split path: the caption text is sent first, then the video media is sent separately.

For example, `https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/1/render%2Emp4?ex=1` now classifies like a normal `.mp4` URL for the Discord caption/video split decision.

## Evidence

Local validation:

- `git diff --check` passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/discord/src/outbound-adapter.test.ts` passed with 1 test file and 48 tests.

Production-path terminal proof:

This proof imports the real Discord outbound adapter and calls `discordOutbound.sendMedia` with the encoded-dot video URL. The only injected part is the final Discord send transport, so the transcript can observe whether the production outbound adapter chooses one combined send or the caption-first/media-second split.

```text
[proof] Discord outbound production adapter with injected Discord send transport
[proof] input mediaUrl=https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/1/render%2Emp4?ex=1
[proof] send call count=2
[proof] call 1: {"target":"channel:redacted-discord-channel","content":"rendered clip","mediaUrl":null,"reply":{"messageId":"reply-1","scope":"all"},"accountId":"default"}
[proof] call 2: {"target":"channel:redacted-discord-channel","content":"","mediaUrl":"https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/1/render%2Emp4?ex=1","reply":{"messageId":"reply-1","scope":"all"},"accountId":"default"}
[proof] returned={"channel":"discord","messageId":"proof-2","channelId":"redacted-discord-channel"}
[proof] PASS: encoded-dot video URL takes caption-first/media-second outbound path
```

Focused behavior covered by the regression test:

```text
mediaUrl = https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/1/render%2Emp4?ex=1
caption send -> sendMessageDiscord(..., "rendered clip", ...)
media send   -> sendMessageDiscord(..., "", { mediaUrl })
```

Call chain / impact:

```text
discordOutbound captioned media send
-> normalizeMediaPathForExtension(mediaUrl)
-> URL pathname extraction
-> video extension check
-> caption/media split decision
```

Scope and sibling surfaces:

- Production diff is limited to `extensions/discord/src/media-detection.ts` and changes only URL pathname normalization before suffix detection.
- The test change extends the existing Discord outbound split test in `extensions/discord/src/outbound-adapter.test.ts` instead of adding a new broad test surface.
- No shared media-core helper is changed; this PR intentionally scopes the fix to Discord's local caption/video split detector.
- Malformed percent encoding still falls back to the original URL pathname, so this does not add a new send-time exception path.

Live-proof note:

- This local environment does not expose Discord live smoke credentials (`DISCORD_*` / `OPENCLAW_*DISCORD*` env vars were absent), and the repository's Discord live QA workflow requires maintainer-level repository access. The terminal proof above exercises the production outbound decision path and redacts the channel id.

Closes #101769

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Markdown beginning with dash-prefixed text such as `---not` or `----` could be mistaken for YAML frontmatter, causing metadata or body content to be parsed, stripped, or dropped.

## Why This Change Was Made

Frontmatter now starts and ends only on complete `---` delimiter lines after BOM and newline normalization. The shared extractor owns that contract, and agent prompt/session loading, workspace and dev templates, Claude bundle commands, hooks, skills, and workshop proposals all use the same implementation instead of copied prefix checks.

target.title: fix(oauth): pass workspace context to resolveProviderIdForAuth on refresh failure
target.body:
> [!NOTE]
> **AI-Assisted Contribution:** This PR was prepared and validated with the assistance of the Antigravity AI coding assistant (Gemini 3.5 Flash).

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where the aliased provider lookup fails to resolve workspace-scoped aliases on OAuth token refresh failures.

**Symptom/Behavior:**
When clearing the last good profile on OAuth refresh failures, the aliased provider ID is resolved using the global context instead of the workspace-specific configuration. Specifically, `resolveProviderIdForAuth(cred.provider)` is called with only one argument, omitting the configuration and workspace directory parameters. This causes `resolveProviderAuthAliasMap` to be called with `undefined` parameters, resulting in a failure to resolve workspace-scoped provider aliases and a failure to delete/clear the incorrect profile ID from `snapshot.lastGood`.

Affected location: `[src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth.ts](file://src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth.ts#L472-L475)` (compiled as `dist/oauth-R_OaG_Ep.js` inside `catch (error)` block):
```typescript
        const snapshot = getRuntimeAuthProfileStoreSnapshot(params.agentDir);
        const providerKey = resolveProviderIdForAuth(cred.provider);
        if (snapshot?.lastGood?.[providerKey] === profileId) {
```

## Why This Change Was Made

Implemented a surgical fix to pass the full configuration and workspace context to `resolveProviderIdForAuth` during OAuth refresh failure cleanup.

**Solution Overview:**
1. Update `resolveApiKeyForProfile` to accept an optional `workspaceDir` parameter.
2. Pass the full parameters (context/config) to `resolveProviderIdForAuth`:
   ```typescript
   const providerKey = resolveProviderIdForAuth(cred.provider, {
     config: cfg,
     workspaceDir: params.workspaceDir,
   });
   ```
3. Thread the `workspaceDir` context through all calling paths (including `src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.ts`, `src/agents/model-auth.ts`, `src/agents/openclaw-plugin-tools.ts`, and `src/plugin-sdk/provider-auth.ts`).

---

## User Impact

Corrects behavior to ensure that when clearing the last good profile on OAuth refresh failures, the aliased provider ID is resolved using the full workspace configuration (`cfg` and `workspaceDir`) to ensure workspace-scoped aliases/plugins are correctly respected. This prevents stale/broken credentials from sticking around as `lastGood` in workspaces using scoped aliases.

---

## Evidence

### Unit Tests / Verification Suite
- Verified that existing related tests (`oauth-refresh-failure.test.ts`, `provider-auth.test.ts`, and `prepare.test.ts`) pass.
- A total of 150 tests passed successfully across the affected surfaces.

target.title: fix(exec): bypass fail-closed interpreter heuristic when security is full
target.body:
## Evidence

**Generated 2026-07-07 from the production `validateScriptFileForShellBleed` function on this branch** using `pnpm exec tsx proof-run.mts` (not a test runner — calls the exported production seam directly):

```
$ pnpm exec tsx proof-run.mts

=== BEFORE: security unset (fail-closed heuristic active) ===
  BLOCKED: cat bad.py | python
    -> exec preflight: complex interpreter invocation detected; refusing to run
       without script preflight validation. Use a direct `python <file>.py` or
       `node <file>.js` command.
  BLOCKED: bash -c "python bad.py"
    -> exec preflight: complex interpreter invocation detected; refusing to run
       without script preflight validation. Use a direct `python <file>.py` or
       `node <file>.js` command.
  PASS: python3 script.py | head -30
    (target path `script.py` extractable → no heuristic, file check runs; passes
     because the file does not exist on this machine)

=== AFTER: security="full" (heuristic bypassed) ===
  ALLOWED: cat bad.py | python
  ALLOWED: bash -c "python bad.py"
  ALLOWED: python3 script.py | head -30
```

The `validateScriptFileForShellBleed` seam is exported from the production module (`src/agents/bash-tools.exec.ts`). The proof script imports and calls it directly — no vitest, no mocking, no test infra. `BLOCKED` = the function throws; `ALLOWED` = the function returns `undefined`. Before/after behavior confirmed on the same machine in the same Node.js session.

---

## What Problem This Solves

When `exec.security` is `"full"` and `exec.ask` is `"on-miss"` (a common production config), `shouldSkipExecScriptPreflight` returns `false` because it requires `ask === "off"`. This causes `validateScriptFileForShellBleed` to run the fail-closed interpreter heuristic even though the operator has explicitly declared full agent trust.

The heuristic blocks commands that contain an interpreter invocation + complex shell syntax (pipe, `&&`, etc.) when the script target path cannot be extracted — for example `cat bad.py | python`, `bash -c "python script.py"`, or `python <(cat bad.py)`. In lower-trust configurations this defensive fail-close is the right call. At `security="full"` it produces false positives for patterns like `python3 script.py | head -30` where a pipeline prevents target extraction but the intent is unambiguous.

**Root cause**: `ask` controls approval prompts; `security` controls trust level. These were conflated in the outer skip check, which required `ask === "off"` before any preflight could be bypassed at `security="full"`.

## Fix

Thread `security` into `validateScriptFileForShellBleed` and guard the fail-closed interpreter heuristic behind `security !== "full"`. File content validation (shell variable injection detection via `$VAR` patterns) is **unchanged** — it still runs for all security levels whenever a target path can be extracted from the command.

Changes:
- `validateScriptFileForShellBleed`: add optional `security?: ExecSecurity` param; wrap the interpreter heuristic in `if (params.security !== "full")`
- Call site: pass `security` through
- Tests: add `it.each(failClosedCases)` blocks verifying each previously-blocked command now resolves when `security: "full"` is passed, covering both `ask=on-miss` and `ask=always`
- Docs: update `docs/tools/exec.md` to state `security=full` bypasses the heuristic regardless of ask mode

## Test plan

- [x] All existing `failClosedCases` still fail with default (no `security`) param — heuristic unchanged for non-full security
- [x] All existing `passCases` still pass
- [x] New tests verify each `failClosedCase` resolves when `security: "full"` is passed (covers ask=on-miss and ask=always)
- [x] Existing `createPreflightTool()` tests still catch `$VAR` patterns — file content validation runs regardless of security level

Fixes #87371

target.title: fix: require exact markdown frontmatter delimiters
target.body:
Closes #101769

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users writing Markdown command, hook, skill, workshop proposal, or metadata files could have content that starts with non-delimiter text like `---not` or `----` interpreted as YAML frontmatter.

That could make OpenClaw read unexpected metadata and strip or alter body text even though the Markdown did not begin with a whole `---` delimiter line.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared markdown-core frontmatter parser now requires exact `---` delimiter lines for both opening and closing fences. Bundled Claude command body extraction and skill workshop proposal stripping now reuse the same shared delimiter extractor instead of keeping separate prefix-based logic.

This keeps metadata parsing and body stripping aligned without adding config, compatibility shims, or plugin-specific policy.

## User Impact

Markdown files can now safely begin with dash-prefixed text that is not a frontmatter delimiter. Valid `---` frontmatter blocks still parse normally, while `---not` and `----` remain part of the Markdown body.

## Evidence

Before the fix, the reported source-level case parsed unexpected metadata:

```text
node --import tsx --input-type=module - <<'EOF'
import { parseFrontmatterBlock } from './packages/markdown-core/src/frontmatter.ts';
const content = '---not\nname: nope\n---not\nbody';
console.log(JSON.stringify(parseFrontmatterBlock(content)));
EOF
{"name":"nope"}
```

After the fix, the final source-level proof keeps invalid delimiter text as Markdown and still accepts a valid block:

```text
node --import tsx --input-type=module - <<'EOF'
import { parseFrontmatterBlock, stripFrontmatterBlock } from './packages/markdown-core/src/frontmatter.ts';
const invalid = '---not\nname: nope\n---not\nbody';
const valid = '---\nname: valid\n---\nbody';
console.log('invalid', JSON.stringify(parseFrontmatterBlock(invalid)), JSON.stringify(stripFrontmatterBlock(invalid)));
console.log('valid', JSON.stringify(parseFrontmatterBlock(valid)), JSON.stringify(stripFrontmatterBlock(valid)));
EOF
invalid {} "---not\nname: nope\n---not\nbody"
valid {"name":"valid"} "body"
```

target.title: fix(googlechat): cap two warn-once Sets via createDedupeCache
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes unbounded memory growth in two Google Chat warn-once deduplication Sets. Both `warnedDeprecatedUsersEmailAllowFrom` and `warnedMutableGroupKeys` accumulated every warned key forever with no eviction, TTL, or size cap.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replaced both unbounded `Set<string>` instances with `createDedupeCache({ ttlMs: 0, maxSize: 4096 })`, imported from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/dedupe-runtime` per extension boundary policy. The `check()` method provides touch-on-read LRU semantics.

## User Impact

No change for gateways handling fewer than 4 096 distinct warned keys per cache.

## Evidence

### Real-path proof — `createDedupeCache` exercised through the real OpenClaw logging system

The script initializes the OpenClaw console logger (`loggingState.overrideSettings`), imports the actual `monitor-access.js` module, and calls `applyGoogleChatInboundAccessPolicy` twice with a deprecated group key. The REAL OpenClaw subsystem logger (not a mock) writes to stderr:

```text
$ node --import tsx monitor-access-proof.mjs 2>&1

[googlechat] Deprecated Google Chat group key detected: group routing now requires stable space ids (spaces/<spaceId>). Update channels.googlechat.groups keys: dk
Call 1: warning fired through real OpenClaw logger (see [googlechat] line above)
Call 2: warning suppressed — createDedupeCache.check() deduplicated
OK: deduplication works through REAL OpenClaw subsystem logger
```

- First call: `warnMutableGroupKeysConfigured` -> real `createDedupeCache.check()` returns false -> warning emitted
- Second call (same key): `createDedupeCache.check()` returns true (cached) -> warning suppressed

<details>
<summary>Proof script (monitor-access-proof.mjs)</summary>

```js
import { loggingState } from "./src/logging/state.js";
loggingState.overrideSettings = { level: "info" };
import { createSubsystemLogger } from "./src/logging/subsystem.js";

const proofLogger = createSubsystemLogger("googlechat/proof");

const { applyGoogleChatInboundAccessPolicy } = await import("./extensions/googlechat/src/monitor-access.js");

const ctx = {

  config: { channels: { googlechat: {} }, commands: { useAccessGroups: true } },

  message: { annotations: [] },
  isGroup: true, senderId: "users/a", senderName: "A", rawBody: "h", logVerbose,
};

try { await applyGoogleChatInboundAccessPolicy(ctx); } catch(e) {}
try { await applyGoogleChatInboundAccessPolicy(ctx); } catch(e) {}
```
</details>

### Cache cap and LRU eviction

target.title: fix(feishu): retry once on token-invalid errors 99991663/99991664 with cache invalidation (fixes #97287)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #97287.

When the cached `tenant_access_token` becomes invalid (e.g. clock drift, server-side revocation, or Feishu token expiry), the plugin cannot send messages. Error code `99991663 Invalid access token` is returned, but the plugin does not automatically refresh the token and retry. Users must manually restart the gateway to recover.

## Changes Made

- `extensions/feishu/src/comment-shared.ts`: Added `addFeishuTokenCacheClearer` / `clearFeishuTokenCaches`. `getFeishuTokenInvalidCode` detects 99991663/99991664. `requestFeishuApi` retries once on token-invalid (`retriedTokenInvalid` flag, independent of rate-limit budget). Fulfilled token-invalid bodies handled.
- `extensions/feishu/src/client.ts`: `createFeishuClient` creates a plugin-owned `Lark.Cache` via `buildSdkTokenCache()`. `clearClientCache` expires `CTenantAccessToken` in the private cache by appId namespace.
- `extensions/feishu/src/send.ts`: getter pattern — `opts.getClient()` inside request closure, ensures fresh client after cache clear.
- `extensions/feishu/src/streaming-card.ts`: `clearFeishuTokenCache` registered. CardKit create retry on 99991663/99991664. Guarded-fetch release on non-JSON response.
- `extensions/feishu/src/client.test.ts`: NEW — client cache isolation tests.
- `extensions/feishu/src/send.retry.test.ts`: NEW — token-invalid + rate-limit retry sequence tests.
- `extensions/feishu/src/streaming-card.test.ts`: NEW/UPDATED — card streaming tests including retry and guarded-fetch release.
- `extensions/feishu/src/token-retry-proof.test.ts`: NEW — end-to-end recovery proof tests (99991663/99991664 detection, cache clearing, getter pattern).

## Evidence

### Live runtime proof (commit: 83830f71ec)

## What Problem This Solves

`resolveHeartbeatPreflight` in `src/infra/heartbeat-runner.ts` read the workspace `HEARTBEAT.md` with an unbounded `fs.readFile`, allowing an arbitrarily large file to be loaded into memory and processed by the heartbeat pipeline.

Oversized `HEARTBEAT.md` files are now treated like missing files: the heartbeat run continues without the file content. Normal-sized heartbeat files behave exactly as before.

target.title: fix(codex): suppress stdout/stderr stream errors in sandbox subprocesses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where stdout/stderr pipe errors from Codex sandbox subprocesses (both process RPC and streaming HTTP helper) could surface as unhandled Node stream errors, crashing the exec-server WebSocket bridge.

## Why This Change Was Made

When a Codex sandbox process exits or its pipes are broken, the Node stream layer emits `error` events on stdout/stderr Readable streams. Without a listener, these bubble into an unhandled rejection that terminates the exec-server bridge. The sibling `http.ts` streaming helper path had the same gap.

The fix mirrors the same pattern used in `src/agents/sessions/exec.ts:177-178`: attach a no-op error listener to suppress the events while letting the process `close` handler remain authoritative.

## User Impact

Codex sandbox exec-server no longer crashes when a subprocess pipe breaks in either the process RPC or streaming HTTP path. Output collection and close signalling continue to work normally.

## Evidence

**processes.ts**: Before the fix, no stdout/stderr stream error listeners at the sandbox subprocess spawn point.

```diff
 const child = spawn(command, args, { env: execSpec.env, stdio: ["pipe", "pipe", "pipe"] });
 managed.child = child;
+// Output pipes may fail independently while the process is running.
+const ignoreOutputStreamError = () => {};
+child.stdout.on("error", ignoreOutputStreamError);
+child.stderr.on("error", ignoreOutputStreamError);
```

**http.ts**: Same gap in the streaming HTTP subprocess spawn path.

```diff
 const child = spawn(command, args, { env: execSpec.env, stdio: ["pipe", "pipe", "pipe"] });
+
+const ignoreOutputStreamError = () => {};
+child.stdout.on("error", ignoreOutputStreamError);
+child.stderr.on("error", ignoreOutputStreamError);
```

**Runtime proof — sandbox exec-server pipe survival regression test**:

A new test file `sandbox-exec-server.pipe-survival.test.ts` exercises the real
sandbox exec-server WebSocket JSON-RPC bridge. The test spawns a child process
writing 200 lines to stdout/stderr, kills it mid-output, and verifies the bridge
survives. A second process confirms full functionality. The HTTP streaming path
is also tested with a local echo server.

```text
$ npx vitest run --project extension-codex sandbox-exec-server.pipe-survival

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (2)
   Duration  3.60s

 ✓ process bridge survives when child writes 200 lines then is killed (1234ms)
 ✓ http streaming bridge survives when socket closes mid-stream (570ms)
```

The same no-op error listener pattern already exists in `src/agents/sessions/exec.ts:177-178`, confirming this is the repo-standard approach.

target.title: fix(discord): dispose fallback timeout abort listeners
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes fallback abort-signal listener cleanup in the active Discord monitor paths. When native `AbortSignal.any` is unavailable, Discord manually attaches abort listeners to parent signals. The queued message runner and media download path were still using the signal-only helper, so successful monitor work could leave parent signals retaining stale fallback listeners.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fallback merged signal now has an explicit disposer, and the active Discord monitor callers use it directly:

- `message-run-queue.ts` disposes the merged job/lifecycle abort signal in `finally` after queued processing settles.
- `message-media.ts` disposes the merged request/timeout abort signal in `finally` after media download settles.
- `runDiscordTaskWithTimeout` keeps the same disposable cleanup for the deprecated timeout compatibility path.

## User Impact

Long-running Discord monitor processes avoid accumulating stale abort listeners across repeated queued message runs and media downloads on runtimes or test environments that take the fallback merge path.

## Evidence

- Collision check before opening: no open PR modified `extensions/discord/src/monitor/timeouts.ts` or `extensions/discord/src/monitor/timeouts.test.ts`.
- ClawSweeper blocker addressed: the two current signal-only monitor callers it identified are now updated to `createDisposableMergedAbortSignal` and dispose in `finally`.
- `git diff --check`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-discord.config.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.queue.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-utils.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/timeouts.test.ts --reporter verbose`

Focused test output:

```text
✓ |extension-discord| extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.queue.test.ts > createDiscordMessageHandler queue behavior > disposes fallback run abort listeners after queued processing settles
✓ |extension-discord| extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-utils.test.ts > resolveMediaList > disposes fallback attachment abort listeners after downloads settle
✓ |extension-discord| extensions/discord/src/monitor/timeouts.test.ts > discord monitor timeouts > disposes fallback merged abort listeners after completed timeout races settle
✓ |extension-discord| extensions/discord/src/monitor/timeouts.test.ts > discord monitor timeouts > does not refire fallback merged abort listeners after timeout races settle

Test Files  3 passed (3)
Tests  81 passed (81)
```

Representative runtime proof, run with `pnpm exec tsx` against the PR branch, not through Vitest: the harness disables native `AbortSignal.any`, creates a real `createDiscordMessageRunQueue`, enqueues a Discord monitor-style job, captures the abort signal passed to `processDiscordMessage`, then aborts the parent signals after queued processing settles.

```text
Discord monitor queue fallback cleanup proof
{
  "nativeAbortSignalAny": "disabled for fallback path",
  "processed": true,
  "parentAbortListenersAdded": 1,
  "parentAbortListenersRemoved": 1,
  "mergedSignalIsFallback": true,
  "mergedSignalBeforeParentAbort": false,
  "mergedSignalAfterParentAbort": false,
  "runtimeErrorCount": 0
}
```

The regression tests and the runtime proof both force the fallback path by temporarily disabling native `AbortSignal.any`. The runtime proof shows the monitor queue path removed the parent abort listener on normal completion, and aborting the parent signal after settlement no longer aborts the captured merged signal.

target.title: fix: add timeout to parent-fork token count resolution (fixes #101718)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`resolveParentForkTokenCount` reads the parent transcript to estimate token count when forking a session, but has **no timeout or abort signal**. On large transcripts (hundreds of MB) or slow filesystems (NFS, FUSE, saturated SSD), this blocks session creation and reply fork paths indefinitely, accumulating blocked async contexts that exhaust gateway connection slots (#101718).

### Call chain

```
sessions.create({ fork: true })
  → session-create-service resolveParentForkDecision
    → session-fork.ts resolveParentForkTokenCount
      → session-fork.runtime.ts resolveParentForkTokenCountRuntime
        (fs.stat + async file read — NO TIMEOUT)
```

## Changes

**2 files, +54/-2 (source: +6; tests: +48)**

**`src/auto-reply/reply/session-fork.ts`** (+6 lines):
- Import `withTimeout` from `../../infra/fs-safe.js`
- Add `PARENT_FORK_TOKEN_TIMEOUT_MS = 2_000` constant
- Wrap `resolveParentForkTokenCountRuntime` in `withTimeout(..., 2_000).catch(() => undefined)`

When the 2-second timeout fires, `resolveParentForkTokenCount` returns `undefined` — the same sentinel the normal fallback path already produces. `resolveParentForkDecision` already handles `undefined` correctly: returns `{status: "fork"}` without `parentTokens` estimate.

This single bounded deadline (recommended by ClawSweeper review) covers all filesystem awaits inside the runtime (fs.stat + transcript read up to 1MB + potential index scan) in one wrapper.

**`src/auto-reply/reply/session-fork.test.ts`** (+48 lines):
- 3 new test cases for `resolveParentForkDecision`:
  1. Fast runtime → returns `fork` with `parentTokens` (50k)
  2. **Hanging runtime → returns `fork` without `parentTokens` within 2s** (timeout proof)
  3. Parent too large → returns `skip`

### Why 2 seconds and not 10?
- The timeout only guards the stale-token filesystem probe after the synchronous `freshPersistedTokens` fast path
- Even on NFS, fs.stat + 1MB tail read should complete in < 500ms
- 2s is aggressive but safe: returning `undefined` (allow fork without estimate) is always better than blocking indefinitely

## Evidence

### Unit tests (18/18 passed)

```
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  18 passed (18)   [4 session-fork + 14 runtime]
   Start at  00:23:08
   Duration  6.63s  (tests 2.27s — confirms 2s timeout exercised)
```

Timeout test specifically runs for ~2008ms, confirming the deadline fires and fork proceeds without blocking.

### Real behavior proof (13/13 passed — Platinum level)

```

  Section 4 — Source Audit: withTimeout IS in session-fork.ts

target.title: fix: antml:/mm: namespaced tool-call XML leaks into chat replies (#97750)
target.body:
Closes #97750

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users on any deployment that serves a Claude model through an anthropic-messages-compatible proxy would see raw tool-call XML in their chat replies, and sometimes get no usable answer at all, when the proxy intermittently degraded a native `tool_use` block into plain text.

In that degraded case the model's tool call arrives as the Anthropic namespaced XML dialect — an optional `function_calls` wrapper containing `antml:invoke` / `antml:parameter` tags that use `name="..."` attributes (MiniMax emits the same shape with an `mm:` prefix). The harness did not recognize the namespace prefix or the attribute form anywhere, so the entire block leaked into the user-visible message instead of being executed, and a turn whose whole body was unrecognized markup could end with no real reply.

A follow-up fix in this PR also closes a streaming-only variant of the same leak: the final repair parser accepts whitespace-flexible attribute-dialect invoke tags (optional whitespace after `<`, around the `name` attribute, and around `=`), but the streamed-prefix recognizer only kept the exact `<ns>invoke name="` form buffered. A grammar-legal split form such as `<invoke name = "exec">` was therefore classified impossible mid-stream and flushed as raw visible text before final-message repair could promote it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The degraded tool call should never reach the user: it should either be executed or, failing that, hidden. This change teaches both layers that own that contract about the namespaced attribute dialect, using a closed namespace allow-list (`antml:`, `mm:`) factored into a single reused fragment — mirroring the existing reasoning-tag handling — so arbitrary `ns:` prefixes are not matched.

- Visible-text sanitizer: the tag-name scan now skips a known namespace prefix before reading the local tag name, and the quick-check / payload-start patterns accept the same optional prefix, so a namespaced wrapper is stripped on the same opt-in paths as the bare dialect.
- Repair/promotion layer: the repair grammar now promotes the attribute dialect (`invoke name="..."` / `parameter name="..."`, optionally namespaced, optionally wrapped in `function_calls`) back into an executed tool call, including the streaming and over-cap paths. Parameterless/self-closing invokes are never promoted, parameter values stay literal, and the existing payload-size limits are honored.
- Streaming-prefix recognizer: `isViableXmlishInvokeOpenPrefix` is rewritten as a phase scanner that mirrors the final parser grammar one token at a time, so a buffer that ends partway through any phase of a grammar-legal invoke open (including whitespace-split forms) stays buffered instead of leaking, while the existing tool-name gating is preserved unchanged.
- Internal delivery paths become code-aware without changing the public contract: the low-level `packages/tool-call-repair` stripper takes an optional code-region predicate, threaded in from the delivery pipeline, `sanitizeUserFacingText`, and the visible-text sanitizer, so a complete invoke block inside a fenced or inline code span is no longer silently removed on those internal paths.
- The exported plugin SDK helper `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` stays strict by default (it scrubs tool-call-shaped blocks even inside code regions, matching current main), preserving the upgrade contract for third-party callers that use it to sanitize untrusted visible text. Code-aware behavior is available as an explicit opt-in via `{ preserveCodeRegions: true }`; the default remains a strict scrubber.

Non-goals/boundaries: the Anthropic and DSML transports are intentionally untouched (the native path is correct; the failure is degraded text owned by the repair package and sanitizer); the exported SDK helper's default behavior is unchanged from main (strict), with code-awareness added only as an opt-in and to internal delivery call sites; and no runtime fallback execution from sanitized text is introduced. The equals dialect (`<function=...>`/`<parameter=...>`), bracket, and Harmony paths are unchanged.

## User Impact

Users on proxied Claude routes no longer see raw `antml:` tool-call XML in their replies. When the proxy degrades a tool call to text, the call is now recovered and executed instead of leaking, so the turn produces a real result. This now also holds when the degraded tool call streams in a whitespace-flexible form split across chunks, which previously slipped past the streamed-prefix recognizer and leaked. Code examples that legitimately contain such tags inside code fences or inline code are preserved rather than stripped.

## Evidence

Focused unit tests cover both layers and the edge cases:

- Sanitizer: namespaced `function_calls`/`invoke`/`parameter` stripped to surrounding prose; truncated namespaced opening hidden; namespaced markup preserved inside fenced and inline code through the full delivery pipeline. Delivery-path regression coverage locks both directions across the `antml:`, `mm:`, and bare (no-namespace) prefixes: an unfenced standalone `invoke` block (and a pure standalone block with no surrounding prose) is stripped, while the same block inside a fenced code span is preserved verbatim, so the real leak shape is removed without over-scrubbing legitimate code examples.
- Promotion: a streamed namespaced attribute-dialect message promotes to a real tool call (including a split/chunked stream); a self-closing parameterless invoke is not promoted; mixed prose declines promotion; an arbitrary `foo:` namespace is neither promoted nor stripped (locks the closed allow-list); multiple invokes in one wrapper parse and strip correctly; a parameter value containing a literal close marker is extracted to the first close.
- Streaming-prefix recognizer: whitespace-split attribute-dialect invoke opens (spaces around the `name` attribute and `=`, including the open tag split across stream chunks at the whitespace boundaries, for both `antml:` and bare namespaces and a single-quote variant) stay buffered and promote to a tool call instead of leaking.
- Argument-less invoke followed by prose: a complete zero-parameter (`<invoke name="read"></invoke>\nHello`) or self-closing (`<invoke name="read"/>\nHello`) invoke followed by visible prose no longer leaks the raw invoke XML in streamed output — the invoke markup is stripped and only the prose (`Hello`) is delivered, with no tool call promoted, across `antml:`, `mm:`, and bare prefixes and split-across-chunks streams. Regression coverage also locks the final-message shapes where the invoke and prose arrive as separate text content blocks, and where a single leading content block carries both the invoke and its trailing prose, so the visible prose is preserved exactly once with no duplication or loss; a pure argument-less invoke with no prose still scrubs to an empty message; and a parametered invoke with no prose still promotes to a tool call (positive lock).

Real-behavior proof (Docker, redacted): a self-contained harness under `proof/pr-97845/` drives the actual stream normalizer through the same option wiring the provider-stream wrapper uses, feeding a degraded provider stream that emits a whitespace-split invoke open (`<invoke name = "exec">...`) split across chunks at the whitespace boundaries. Captured runtime output shows the regression and its fix:

With the recognizer reverted to its previous literal-prefix form (BEFORE), the split open leaks as visible text:

```
fake upstream chunks: ["<invoke"," name"," ="," \"exec\">","<parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter>","</invoke>"]
emitted events:
  [1] text_delta "<invoke"
  [2] text_delta " name"
  [3] text_delta " ="
  [4] text_delta " \"exec\">"
  [5] text_delta "<parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter>"
  [6] text_delta "</invoke>"
  [7] toolcall_start ...
visible text emitted to user: "<invoke name = \"exec\"><parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter></invoke>"
VERDICT: LEAK
```

With the fix in place (AFTER), the same bytes stay buffered and promote to a tool call with no visible leak:

```
emitted events:
  [0] toolcall_start
  [1] toolcall_delta {"command":"echo demo"}
  [2] done reason=toolUse  toolCall name=exec arguments={"command":"echo demo"}
visible text emitted to user: ""
VERDICT: NO LEAK
```

The captured output above is the redacted before/after runtime evidence; the synthetic stream reproduction needs no provider key. (The proof was produced with a Docker harness that drives the real stream normalizer through the provider-stream wrapper; per review feedback it is kept here in the description rather than committed to the branch.)

Exported SDK helper contract (strict default): the `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` tests lock both modes — with no options the helper strips a tool-call-shaped block even when it sits inside a Markdown code fence or inline span (strict scrubber, matching main), while `{ preserveCodeRegions: true }` preserves the same fenced/inline example verbatim. Coverage spans namespaced/plain/zero-parameter/self-closing forms and a mixed fenced+unfenced case where the default strips both and the opt-in spares only the fenced sibling, so the public upgrade contract cannot silently regress.

```

target.title: fix(security): bound plugin manifest reads in audit deep scan
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`readPluginManifestExtensions` in `src/security/audit-extra.async.ts` read each installed plugin's `package.json` with an unbounded `fs.readFile`. A malicious or broken plugin could place an arbitrarily large manifest in the plugin directory and exhaust memory or slow the security audit.

## Why This Change Was Made

The audit deep scan now enforces a hard 1 MiB size limit on plugin `package.json` reads, using the existing `statRegularFile` / `readRegularFile` helpers from `src/infra/regular-file.js`, which also reject symlinks and non-file targets. Oversized manifests throw a clear error that surfaces as a `plugins.code_safety.manifest_parse_error` finding, matching the existing malformed-JSON behavior so the issue is visible instead of silently skipped.

## User Impact

Users will receive a clear security audit warning if any installed plugin manifest exceeds 1 MiB, and the audit will no longer attempt to load unbounded file content during deep scan.

## Evidence

- Added a regression test in `src/security/audit-extra.async.test.ts` that creates a `package.json` of `1 MiB + 1` bytes and asserts a `manifest_parse_error` finding is emitted for the oversized plugin.

target.title: fix(security): bound mcporter registry read in audit
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`readGlobalMcporterRegistrySummary` in `src/security/audit.ts` read the global MCP registry (`stateDir/skills/config/mcporter.json`) with an unbounded `fs.readFile`, so a maliciously large or corrupted registry could exhaust memory during a security audit.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replaced the unbounded read with `readRegularFile`, which rejects symlinks and non-files and supports a byte cap. A 16 MiB limit is consistent with other bounded config reads in the codebase. If the file exceeds the limit or cannot be read, the function returns `null`, treating the oversized registry the same as a missing one.

## User Impact

Security audit no longer buffers an unbounded registry file into memory; behavior is unchanged for normal-sized registries.

target.title: feat(signal): add setup wizard container flow
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where Signal setup required users to hand-configure native `signal-cli` even when they wanted OpenClaw to guide them through a local Signal REST container or an existing Signal API server. It also fixes setup/status gaps where Signal transport mode, receive readiness, and multi-account setup state could be misreported or persisted on the wrong account.

## Why This Change Was Made

Signal setup now owns native, Docker container, and existing-server setup paths inside the Signal plugin, while core setup gains only the generic `setupApplied` rollback signal needed to avoid persisting failed or cancelled setup attempts. Managed Docker setup now verifies the account-specific `/v1/receive/{account}` WebSocket before saving container setup, so an account-list response alone is not treated as a working Signal setup.

## User Impact

Users can configure Signal through the setup wizard with a Docker container flow, QR/linking guidance, and existing-server reconfiguration that does not require re-entering an already saved Signal number. Operators get clearer `channels status` output for ready, account-missing, receive-unavailable, and unreachable Signal states, and mixed multi-account configs keep transport fields scoped to the intended account.

## Evidence

Behavioral proof:

- Docker setup now verifies `/v1/receive/{account}` before every managed setup success return: single listed account, selected account from multiple linked accounts, and newly linked QR account.
- Non-interactive existing-server setup resets stale Docker transport state to `apiMode: "auto"` and `autoStart: false`, so a previous container setup does not force a later `--http-url` config through the container adapter.
- Non-interactive native setup resets stale Docker transport state to `apiMode: "native"`, `autoStart: true`, and clears `httpUrl`, so a later `--cli-path`/host/port setup does not keep using an old external server.
- Failed or cancelled setup returns `setupApplied: false`, so core setup skips account selection hooks, setup callbacks, completion notes, and partial config persistence for unsuccessful setup attempts.
- Signal status/probe output now exposes readiness-specific states instead of collapsing account-missing or receive-unavailable probes into generic working/unreachable output.
- Screenshots are omitted because this PR changes terminal/setup wizard and gateway status behavior; the reviewer-checkable proof is the command/test output and config transition coverage below.

Automated checks run on the final target:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/signal/src/core.test.ts extensions/signal/src/setup-core.test.ts` passed: 2 files, 109 tests.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.extensions.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/extensions.tsbuildinfo` passed.
- `pnpm config:docs:check` passed before the ClawSweeper receive-readiness fix; this fix did not touch generated config docs.
- `node --import tsx scripts/generate-bundled-channel-config-metadata.ts --check` passed before the ClawSweeper receive-readiness fix; this fix did not touch bundled channel metadata.
- `node --max-old-space-size=8192 --import tsx scripts/generate-plugin-sdk-api-baseline.ts --check` passed before the ClawSweeper receive-readiness fix; this fix did not touch SDK API exports.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` passed.
- Native review phase: `codex review --base origin/main` returned clean before ClawSweeper requested the receive-readiness hardening.
- Cold review phase: one independent cold review of `origin/main...HEAD` returned no actionable findings before ClawSweeper requested the receive-readiness hardening.
- ClawSweeper iter 1 found the receive-readiness gap; this branch now fixes that finding and adds focused regressions for the three Docker setup success paths.

Safety: this proof did not touch real `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json`, did not send Signal messages, and did not start arbitrary OpenClaw agents.

## Summary

This PR tightens the existing compatible-bundle MCP path for bundles that need a narrower default tool surface.

- Adds regression coverage that a Codex-compatible bundle `.mcp.json` preserves `toolFilter.include`, `toolFilter.exclude`, and a relative bundle data root.
- Documents bundle MCP tool filters on the plugin-bundles page alongside the existing transport and tool-naming guidance.
- Keeps scope limited to bundle MCP loading/docs; runtime filtering behavior already exists and is covered separately.

Reviewers should focus on whether the bundle MCP docs accurately describe the existing runtime behavior and whether the new compatible-bundle regression is useful.

## Linked context

No issue filed.

Related precedent investigated: bundle MCP support and follow-up coverage in prior OpenClaw PRs such as #48611, #71287, #79686, and #88399. This PR follows that existing bundle MCP seam.
